key_insight: Open-weight LLMs can reliably convert CAV vulnerability text into structured STIX and CWE outputs, but full attack-technique mapping is still difficult.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more standardized threat intelligence for autonomous vehicle security teams to prioritize vulnerabilities and defenses.
method: Built CAV-STIXGen from CAV CVE descriptions mapped to STIX SDO/SRO, CWE, and MITRE ATT&CK labels
Benchmarked 11 open-weight LLMs from 4B to 120B parameters across prompting strategies and temperatures
Compared single-model and multi-agent setups, and analyzed CWE/ATT&CK co-occurrence patterns
evidence_signal: The best single-model results reached F1 = 0.94 for SDO, 0.63 for SRO, and 0.99 for CWE mapping, while MITRE ATT&CK mapping remained challenging.
watch_item: SRO and especially full ATT&CK mapping are less reliable, so human review is still needed before operational use.
paper_title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Generating Structured Threat Information for Autonomous Vehicle Vulnerabilities
